title: One Can Short
summary: A shopkeeper counts her cans every night, and every morning one has vanished from behind a bolted door.

beats.text: Every morning, one can was missing. My shop was bolted from inside.
Forty cans Monday. Thirty-nine Tuesday. Someone was eating my food.
I sat up all night with a bat.
Outside, the infected pressed my shutters, drawn by light. I switched the torch off.
At three, a tiny scratch came from the stockroom. Smaller than theirs.
The stockroom door was open one inch. Two eyes shone back.
A small voice whispered, "Please don't shout. They hear shouting."
beats.speaker: girl

beats.text: She was six, hiding since the first night, eating one can a day.
I was angry for one second. Then I opened peaches and found a second spoon.
"There are three of us," she whispered.
beats.speaker: girl

beats.text: The freezer door rattled. A scruffy dog crawled out, wagging, and licked the syrup.
